etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: Learned borrowing from Latin ōrnātus, perfect passive participle of ōrnō (“to equip, adorn”), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix). Doublet of orné.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From Latin ōrnātus, perfect passive participle of ōrnō (“to equip, adorn”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix). Compare French orner.
senses: (obsolete) To adorn or honour (someone or something).
